title: Monomial etale charts of regular log-smooth schemes over a trait
statement:
A trait is $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R$ a Noetherian local domain of dimension one whose maximal ideal is principal; a uniformizer $\pi$ is a generator of that maximal ideal.

Use fs log structures, charts and log morphisms as in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. The canonical log structure on a trait is the subsheaf of $\mathcal O_S$ of sections invertible on its generic point; a uniformizer gives its chart $\mathbf N\to R$. In this statement, log smooth over that trait has its fs chart meaning: etale locally on source and target there are compatible charts $\mathbf N\to P$ with $P$ fine saturated, the group map injective with torsion in its cokernel of finite order invertible on the source, such that the induced scheme map to $S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[\mathbf N]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]$ is smooth. Here $\mathbf Z[P]$ is the free abelian group on $P$ with multiplication induced by the monoid law.

Let $(X,M)\to S$ be such an fs log-smooth morphism with $X$ regular Noetherian [def-weil-regular-scheme]. For every point $x\in X$ and every uniformizer $\pi$ of $R$, there exist a regular affine Noetherian scheme $U$, an etale morphism $a:U\to X$, a point $u\in U$ with $a(u)=x$, an integer $n\geq1$, nonnegative integers $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ not all zero, and an etale $S$-morphism
$$b:U\longrightarrow T=\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]/(T_1^{e_1}\cdots T_n^{e_n}-\pi)\bigr).$$
Here etale has the meaning of [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $\operatorname{Spec}$ is [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 3.6.5, printed p.253, using Proposition 3.6.3, printed p.252; canonical trait log structure in Definition 3.6.1.

proof.text: The canonically logged trait is log regular: at its closed point the nonunit ideal is $(\pi)$, its quotient is the residue field (dimension zero), and the characteristic is $\mathbf N$, of rank one; at its generic point the log structure is trivial and the local ring is a field. These give precisely the stratum and dimension conditions. Apply log-smooth preservation of log regularity to $(X,M)\to S$. The chart hypothesis is exactly the one in the statement, including invertible torsion, so $(X,M)$ is log regular.

source.place: Expose VI 1.2, 1.8, printed pp.69--70; XVI 3.6.1 and the log-regularity invocation in 3.6.5.

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$ and the given uniformizer $\pi$. The hypothesis on $(X,M)\to S$ is log smoothness in the sense of [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]: its charts $\mathbf N\to P$ have injective group map, so the kernel is zero, and the torsion of the cokernel is finite of invertible order with smooth comparison. Choose an algebraic closure of $\kappa(x)$ and hence a geometric point $\bar x$ over $x$. Apply the uniformizer-chart theorem for log-smooth schemes over a trait to $V=X$, $\bar v=\bar x$ and the given $\pi$. It gives an etale $a:W\to X$ whose image contains $x$, a fine saturated monoid $P$ with torsion-free $P^{\rm gp}$, an injection $g:\mathbf N\to P$, a chart $P\to M|_W$ compatible through $g$ with the chart $1\mapsto\pi$ of $S$, and an etale comparison $c:W\to S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[\mathbf N]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]$. Choose $w\in W$ with $a(w)=x$ and, by the same algebraic-closure statement, a geometric point $\bar w$ over $w$. Since $a$ is etale it is locally of finite presentation and hence locally of finite type; $W$ is locally Noetherian by the cited finite-type lemma.

source.place: Expose XVI 3.6.3 with Q=N (footnote x) and first paragraph of proof of 3.6.5, printed pp.252--253; local Noetherian input: Stacks Tag 01T6, morphisms.tex, lemma-finite-type-noetherian.

proof.text: Give $W$ the pulled-back log structure. The map $a$ is strict: on a pulled-back chart its monoid map is the identity, its group cokernel is zero, and its comparison is the etale morphism $a$, which is smooth by the cited etale-smoothness lemma. Log-smooth preservation therefore makes $W$ log regular. At every geometric point of $W$, its characteristic equals the characteristic at the corresponding geometric point of $X$, because $a$ is etale and the log structure is the inverse-image sheaf. As $X$ is regular and log regular, the free-characteristic criterion makes these monoids free. The converse direction of the same criterion on $W$ makes every ordinary local ring of $W$ regular. Thus $W$ is regular; subsequent open restrictions remain regular and locally Noetherian.

source.place: Expose VI 1.7--1.8, printed p.70; XVI proof of 3.6.5, regular and log-regular source.

proof.text: Let $F\subset P$ be the elements whose chart images are units at $\bar w$. It is a face: in a local ring a product is a unit exactly when both factors are units. Choose finite monoid generators of $P$. The generators lying in $F$ generate $F$, since the face property applied to an expression for an element of $F$ forces every summand to lie in $F$. Shrink $W$ to the intersection of the finitely many opens where these images are invertible. Replace $P$ by $P_F=\{p-f:p\in P,f\in F\}$. The face-sharpening lemma says that it is fs and its unit group is $H=F^{\rm gp}$; its group completion is still $P^{\rm gp}$, as both contain $P$ and are subgroups of that group. The chart extends by inverting these units. On monoid rings this is localization at the corresponding monomials, so the new toric model is an open of the old one and $c$ factors through it. The factor is etale by etale cancellation with that open immersion.

source.place: Expose XVI proof of 3.6.5, second paragraph and footnote xi, printed p.253; face localization: Expose VIII 3.1.1--3.1.2.

proof.text: For the localized chart write $P$ again. Its elements mapping to units at $\bar w$ are exactly $H=P^\times$: if $p-f$ maps to a unit, then $p\in F$, so $p-f\in F^{\rm gp}$. The stalk chart identity is $M_{\bar w}=P\oplus_H\mathcal O_{W,\bar w}^{\times}$. Quotienting by the units therefore identifies $P/H$ with $\overline M_{\bar w}$. By regularity and log regularity of $W$, the free-characteristic criterion gives an isomorphism $P/H\cong\mathbf N^r$ for some $r\geq0$.

source.place: Expose XVI proof of 3.6.5, characteristic quotient and free-monoid criterion, printed p.253; VI 1.7.

proof.text: Lift the $r$ standard generators of $P/H$ to elements $v_1,\ldots,v_r\in P$. Define $\phi:\mathbf N^r\oplus H\to P$ by $(m,h)\mapsto\sum_i m_iv_i+h$. It is surjective: subtracting the lift of the image of $p$ in $P/H$ leaves an element of $H$ in $P^{\rm gp}$, and that element, being a unit, belongs to $P$. It is injective: equality first gives equality of the $\mathbf N^r$ coordinates in $P/H$, and cancellation in $P^{\rm gp}$ then gives equality of the $H$ coordinates. Thus $\phi$ is an isomorphism. The group $H$ is finitely generated by the generators of $F$ from Step 4 and torsion-free because it is a subgroup of the torsion-free $P^{\rm gp}$. Use the finite-basis theorem to choose a basis $a_1,\ldots,a_s$ of $H$. Write $g(1)=(e_1,\ldots,e_r,\sum_j f_ja_j)$; all $e_i\geq0$. Replace $a_j$ by $-a_j$ whenever $f_j<0$, making every $f_j\geq0$. Since $g$ is injective, $g(1)\ne0$, so $n=r+s\geq1$ and the tuple $(e_1,\ldots,e_r,f_1,\ldots,f_s)$ is not all zero.

source.place: Expose XVI proof of 3.6.5, splitting of the free quotient and choice of unit-group basis, printed p.253; the cancellation argument is written out.

proof.text: The chart decomposition identifies its monoid ring with $\mathbf Z[t_1,\ldots,t_r,y_1^{\pm1},\ldots,y_s^{\pm1}]$: the monomial indexed by $(m,\sum_jb_ja_j)$ goes to $t^my^b$, giving inverse maps on these abelian-group bases and preserving products. Under this identification $z^{g(1)}=\prod_i t_i^{e_i}\prod_j y_j^{f_j}$. Tensoring over $\mathbf Z[\mathbf N]=\mathbf Z[q]$ with $R$, where $q\mapsto\pi$, therefore gives the ring $B=R[t_1,\ldots,t_r,y_1^{\pm1},\ldots,y_s^{\pm1}]/(\prod_i t_i^{e_i}\prod_jy_j^{f_j}-\pi)$. Explicitly the two maps are induced by the same variables, subject to the relation $z^{g(1)}=\pi$, and are mutual inverses. Thus the comparison target is $\operatorname{Spec}B$, the principal open where $y_1\cdots y_s$ is invertible in the required monomial hypersurface $T$. If $s=0$, this open is all of $T$. All identifications respect $R$, so the composite $b:W\to\operatorname{Spec}B\hookrightarrow T$ is an $S$-morphism.

source.place: Expose XVI final paragraph of proof of 3.6.5, printed p.253; explicit monoid-ring identification and open torus locus.

proof.text: The map $b$ is etale, being the composite of the etale comparison with an open immersion. Since $W$ is regular, the definition of a regular scheme supplies an affine open neighbourhood $U$ of the underlying point $w$ of $\bar w$ with regular Noetherian coordinate ring. Thus $U$ is regular affine Noetherian. Restricting both $a$ and $b$ along this open immersion preserves etaleness by the cited composition lemma. The point $u=w\in U$ maps to $x$, the exponent tuple is the one in Step 6, and the restricted $b$ is over the original trait $S$. This proves every clause for the chosen $x$ and $\pi$. If $X$ is empty the pointwise assertion is vacuous.

source.place: Expose XVI conclusion of proof of 3.6.5, printed p.253; affine shrinking from the definition of regular scheme; etale composition and open immersions: Stacks morphisms.tex, lemma-composition-etale and lemma-open-immersion-etale.

Steps checked:
- Step 1: the canonical trait is log regular at both points.
- Step 3: W is strict, hence log regular, and regular through both directions of the VI 1.7 criterion.
- Step 4: F is a face, and face-sharpening gives P_F fs with units F^gp; the chart extends and c is étale by cancellation.
- Step 5: P/H is the characteristic monoid and is free.
- Step 6: P is N^r plus H, a basis exists, sign flips make all exponents nonnegative, and g(1)≠0.
- Step 7: the correct comparison target is the torus-open principal open of V(S,π,e), not V itself.
- Step 8: shrinking to a regular affine open.
Edge cases tested: generic point with r=0, s=0, n=1, and invertible torsion P=N with g(1)=d (this rules out the torsion-free trf preservation lemma).
